title: Yankees’ Cody Bellinger wins All-Star Game MVP with 2-RBI night
content:
PHILADELPHIA — His team was booed all week, clearly no love lost between the Philadelphia faithful and the Bronx after the 2009 World Series, but New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger turned those heckles into an All-Star Game MVP award on Tuesday night in the City of Brotherly Love.

Making the start in right field in place of teammate Aaron Judge (right rib stress fracture) and the Minnesota Twins’ Byron Buxton (right hip strain), Bellinger made the most of his moment in the American League’s 4-0 win over the National League at Citizens Bank Park.

Facing NL Cy Young Award candidate Cristopher Sánchez in the first inning, Bellinger turned on a middle-middle sinker for a two-run single into center field. It helped set the tone for the AL in what was mostly an uneventful game.

He finished 1-for-3 with two RBIs, but that was enough to win the coveted prize. Bellinger said on the field after the game that he didn’t expect that first-inning hit to result in an MVP award. “The pitching was just absolutely dominant,” he said.

Hall of Famer Mike Schmidt, a 12-time All-Star, presented the MVP award to Bellinger, who was accompanied by his family when accepting it.

It’s the Yankees’ third All-Star Game MVP award and the club’s first since Giancarlo Stanton in 2022.

Bellinger’s Yankees teammate Ben Rice, also in the starting lineup, chipped in an RBI single of his own in the first to give the AL a 3-0 lead. That was all of the scoring in the game until Miguel Vargas of the Chicago White Sox hit a solo homer in the eighth.

A three-time All-Star, Bellinger was appearing in the Midsummer Classic for the first time since winning the NL MVP as a Los Angeles Dodger in 2019.

This season, he’s posted a 114 OPS+ while playing solid defense all around the field for the Yankees. It is his second season in New York and first since signing a five-year, $162.5 million deal in the offseason to remain in the Bronx.
